global_silver_linings.title: Once Gone From Ireland, Majestic Sea Eagles Continue Their Comeback with Rare New Chick
global_silver_linings.snippet: More than a century after the country’s largest bird of prey disappeared entirely from Ireland, a white-tailed sea eagle has been delivered—and the young fledgling became another success for conservationists to celebrate. Fota Wildlife Park in County Cork has announced the successful birth and fledging of a white-tailed sea eagle chick—the first chick of the […] The post Once Gone From Ireland, Majestic Sea Eagles Continue Their Comeback with Rare New Chick appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: After decades of absence, white-tailed sea eagles are reclaiming their place in Ireland's skies — and every new chick born is proof that patient, dedicated conservation work can genuinely reverse the losses of the past. Nature, given even half a chance, has a remarkable will to return.

discovery_articles.title: Feria de Madrid Mural in Madrid, Spain
discovery_articles.snippet: If you’ve ever taken the metro to or from Madrid airport, you’ve probably noticed the huge mural that adorns the platforms of the station closest to the airport, formerly called Campo de las Naciones and now Feria de Madrid. The Feria de Madrid station was renamed in 2017 to emphasize its importance during the IFEMA (which is the acronym for Institución Ferial de Madrid) events. The metro offers a convenient way to reach this strategic location, with ridership increasing from 3,898 on a normal day to 21,083 during major fairs such as FITUR (Madrid International Tourism Fair).
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Hidden in plain sight beneath one of Europe's busiest airports is a mural so vast it transforms a daily commute into something approaching a gallery visit — yet most travelers rushing to catch flights never quite see it. On fair days, the station swells to five times its usual crowd, a temporary city materializing underground.

discovery_articles.title: Kongo Gumi in Osaka, Japan
discovery_articles.snippet: Japan is home to about two dozen businesses over a thousand years old, including Keiunkan ( https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/nishiyama-onsen-keiunkan ) and Wasuke ( https://www.atlasobscura.com/places/ichimonjiya-wasuke ). Osaka-based construction company Kongo Gumi is the oldest of those, and the oldest company in the entire world. Its history goes all the way back to 578 AD.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Kongo Gumi was quietly building Buddhist temples in Osaka for over 1,400 years — outlasting empires, plagues, and world wars — before finally being absorbed by a larger company in 2006, which feels like the saddest possible ending for the world's oldest business.

discovery_articles.title: The Torment of Saint Anthony in Fort Worth, Texas
discovery_articles.snippet: At twelve or thirteen years old, Michelangelo was already showing signs of being one of the greatest artists the world would ever know. Apprenticing under the prominent Florentine painter Domenico Ghirlandaio, he created a work so masterful that for centuries it was believed to be that of his master. The Torment of Saint Anthony, a religious scene painted around 1487, was based on a print by Martin Schöngauer.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: A boy of twelve painted something so technically astonishing that experts spent centuries insisting it must have been made by a grown master — which raises the quietly unsettling question of how many other child prodigies history has simply credited to the nearest adult.

discovery_articles.title: Tousu at Tofuku-ji Temple in Kyoto, Japan
discovery_articles.snippet: The oldest surviving toilet in Japan can be found at Tofuku-ji, a major Zen temple in Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto. Dating back to the early Muromachi period (1336–1573), this historic restroom is over 500 years old. Known as tousu , this type of toilet is one of the seven facilities that comprise a Zen temple complex.
discovery_articles.ferns_note: Japan's oldest surviving toilet is not tucked away in a museum but still standing inside a functioning Zen temple, a quiet reminder that for medieval monks, answering nature's call was considered a spiritual practice worthy of sacred architecture.

featured_read.title: Hannah Arendt on Love and How to Live with the Fundamental Fear of Loss
featured_read.snippet: “Fearlessness is what love seeks… Such fearlessness exists only in the complete calm that can no longer be shaken by events expected of the future… Hence the only valid tense is the present, the Now.”
featured_read.blurb: Arendt argues that love isn't a feeling that conquers fear but a radical act of presence that renders the future irrelevant — which is either the most comforting or the most demanding idea you'll sit with all week. Pour something warm before you start.

news.title: Sicilian Pizza
news.snippet: Sicilian-style pizza is hard to pin down. In Sicily, it’s called sfincione. True Sicilian-style pizza is spongey, has a red sauce and breadcrumb topping, a light amount of cheese, and usually features anchovies.
news.blurb: A delicious deep-dive into sfincione's spongy, sauce-laden soul — and why Sicilian pizza deserves far more than a footnote on your menu.

news.title: ‘Lip-smackingly sour’: the best (and worst) supermarket cottage cheeses, tasted and rated
news.snippet: Creamy, high-protein and all over our socials, cottage cheese is having a moment. We test the best … • The best supermarket vine tomatoes When I was growing up, cottage cheese was tasteless and mostly only eaten by dieters. Its recent revival in the UK, most likely driven by social media, has similar health reasons at its root – the current protein obsession in gym bros and weight watchers alike – but cottage cheese has become cool .
news.blurb: Cottage cheese has quietly glow'd up from sad diet food to creamy, protein-rich staple, and The Guardian's tasting notes will tell you exactly which tub to reach for.
